blockers.description: The plan's own verify method for Task 3 requires an off-box `nc -z` probe against Traefik's NodePort (30104) to fail AND the new KANBAN-INGRESS mangle-table DROP counter to increase. Netcup's own outer Cloud Firewall (Layer 2, SCP-panel-managed, outside git/SSH/CLI access) already blocks port 30104 from the public internet before packets ever reach the VM's iptables — so the off-box probe times out for the RIGHT reason (Layer 2 blocks it) but the counter cannot increase, because a packet Layer 2 drops never reaches the Layer 3 rule being tested. This is a structural proof-method gap, not a firewall defect: the same problem happened once before (quick task 260906-feq, documented in docs/INFRA_RUNBOOK.md line 175) and was solved by temporarily opening a scoped Netcup console rule for the probe source IP, then closing it again immediately after.
blockers.workaround: Three options presented to operator: (1) operator opens a temporary Netcup SCP console rule for port 30104 from the executor's probe source IP, mirroring the 260906-feq precedent exactly — recommended, most faithful to the plan's actual proof method; (2) accept a weaker, explicitly-documented substitute proof (e.g. a same-VM synthetic packet injection instead of a genuine off-box probe); (3) operator personally runs the off-box probe from a network path Layer 2 already permits, while the executor watches the counter over SSH. Operator has not yet chosen between these — this is what /gsd-pause-work is being invoked to preserve.

human_actions_pending.action: Choose option 1, 2, or 3 above for resolving the off-box-probe-vs-Layer-2-firewall proof gap for 13-08 Task 3, OR (if choosing option 1) open the temporary Netcup SCP console rule yourself and tell the resumed session the probe source IP and that the rule is live.
human_actions_pending.context: Nothing production-affecting is at risk either way — the firewall rule is already live, correct, and verified via `check`; no dead-man timer is armed. context_notes: This is NOT a technical blocker in the sense of something broken — the firewall itself is live, correct, and already verified via the `check` subcommand including surviving a k3s restart. The blocker is purely evidentiary: the plan demands a specific proof method (off-box probe + packet-counter attribution) that Netcup's separate, outer Cloud Firewall (Layer 2, console-only, no API/CLI access from here) structurally prevents by blocking the same traffic one layer earlier.
